audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 13, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Amnon's obsession, Jonadab's grooming plan, David's facilitating command, Tamar's labor and resistance, rape, expulsion, servant participation, survivor lament, Absalom's silencing, David's inaction, revenge killing, false report, flight, and royal grief.

verses.restored: After this, Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and Amnon son of David claimed love for her.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.

modern.text: After some time, David’s son Amnon fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of David’s son Absalom.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֗ן וּלְאַבְשָׁל֧וֹם בֶּן דָּוִ֛ד אָח֥וֹת יָפָ֖ה וּשְׁמָ֣הּ תָּמָ֑ר וַיֶּאֱהָבֶ֖הָ אַמְנ֥וֹן בֶּן דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: Amnon was distressed until he made himself ill because of Tamar his sister. She was a virgin, and it seemed difficult in eyes of Amnon to do anything to her.

familiar.text: And Amnon was so vexed, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and Amnon thought it hard for him to do anything to her.

modern.text: Amnon was sick with frustration over his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed implausible for him to do anything to her.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨צֶר לְאַמְנ֜וֹן לְהִתְחַלּ֗וֹת בַּֽעֲבוּר֙ תָּמָ֣ר אֲחֹת֔וֹ כִּ֥י בְתוּלָ֖ה הִ֑יא וַיִּפָּלֵא֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַמְנ֔וֹן לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָ֖הּ מְאֽוּמָה

verses.restored: Amnon had a companion named Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother. Jonadab was a very cunning man.

familiar.text: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother: and Jonadab was a very subtil man.

modern.text: Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah. Jonadab was a very shrewd man,

original.text: וּלְאַמְנ֣וֹן רֵ֗עַ וּשְׁמוֹ֙ יֽוֹנָדָ֔ב בֶּן שִׁמְעָ֖ה אֲחִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וְי֣וֹנָדָ֔ב אִ֥ישׁ חָכָ֖ם מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: He said to him, Why are you, son of king, becoming thin morning by morning? Will you not tell me? Amnon said, I love Tamar, sister of Absalom my brother.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Why art thou, being the king’s son, lean from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.

modern.text: so he asked Amnon, “Why are you, the son of the king, so depressed morning after morning? Won’t you tell me?” Amnon replied, “I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ מַדּ֣וּעַ אַ֠תָּה כָּ֣כָה דַּ֤ל בֶּן הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר הֲל֖וֹא תַּגִּ֣יד לִ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אַמְנ֔וֹן אֶת תָּמָ֗ר אֲח֛וֹת אַבְשָׁלֹ֥ם אָחִ֖י אֲנִ֥י אֹהֵֽב

verses.restored: Jonadab said, Lie upon your bed and make yourself sick. When your father comes to see you, say, Please let Tamar my sister come and give me bread, preparing food before my eyes so I may see and eat from her hand.

familiar.text: And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and make thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me meat, and dress the meat in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it at her hand.

modern.text: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend you are ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare it in my sight so I may watch her and eat it from her hand.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יְה֣וֹנָדָ֔ב שְׁכַ֥ב עַל מִשְׁכָּבְךָ֖ וְהִתְחָ֑ל וּבָ֧א אָבִ֣יךָ לִרְאוֹתֶ֗ךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֡יו תָּ֣בֹא נָא֩ תָמָ֨ר אֲחוֹתִ֜י וְתַבְרֵ֣נִי לֶ֗חֶם וְעָשְׂתָ֤ה לְעֵינַי֙ אֶת הַבִּרְיָ֔ה לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶרְאֶ֔ה וְאָכַלְתִּ֖י מִיָּדָֽהּ

verses.restored: Amnon lay down and made himself sick. King came to see him. Amnon said to king, Please let Tamar my sister come and make two heart-cakes before my eyes, that I may eat from her hand.

familiar.text: So Amnon lay down, and made himself sick: and when the king was come to see him, Amnon said unto the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat at her hand.

modern.text: So Amnon lay down and feigned illness. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אַמְנ֖וֹן וַיִּתְחָ֑ל וַיָּבֹ֨א הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לִרְאֹת֗וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַמְנ֤וֹן אֶל הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ תָּֽבוֹא נָ֞א תָּמָ֣ר אֲחֹתִ֗י וּתְלַבֵּ֤ב לְעֵינַי֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י לְבִב֔וֹת וְאֶבְרֶ֖ה מִיָּדָֽהּ

verses.restored: David sent to Tamar at house, saying, Please go to house of Amnon your brother and prepare food for him.

familiar.text: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to thy brother Amnon’s house, and dress him meat.

modern.text: Then David sent word to Tamar at the palace: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶל תָּמָ֖ר הַבַּ֣יְתָה לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכִ֣י נָ֗א בֵּ֚ית אַמְנ֣וֹן אָחִ֔יךְ וַעֲשִׂי ל֖וֹ הַבִּרְיָֽה

verses.restored: Tamar went to house of Amnon her brother while he lay down. She took dough, kneaded it, shaped cakes before his eyes, and cooked them.

familiar.text: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was laid down. And she took flour, and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and did bake the cakes.

modern.text: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked them.

original.text: וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ תָּמָ֗ר בֵּ֛ית אַמְנ֥וֹן אָחִ֖יהָ וְה֣וּא שֹׁכֵ֑ב וַתִּקַּ֨ח אֶת הַבָּצֵ֤ק ותלוש וַתְּלַבֵּ֣ב לְעֵינָ֔יו וַתְּבַשֵּׁ֖ל אֶת הַלְּבִבֽוֹת

verses.restored: She took pan and poured them before him, but he refused to eat. Amnon said, Send every man out from me. Every man went out from him.

familiar.text: And she took a pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they went out every man from him.

modern.text: Then she brought the pan and set it down before him, but he refused to eat. “Send everyone away!” said Amnon. And everyone went out.

original.text: וַתִּקַּ֤ח אֶת הַמַּשְׂרֵת֙ וַתִּצֹ֣ק לְפָנָ֔יו וַיְמָאֵ֖ן לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַמְנ֗וֹן הוֹצִ֤יאוּ כָל אִישׁ֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י וַיֵּצְא֥וּ כָל אִ֖ישׁ מֵעָלָֽיו

verses.restored: Amnon said to Tamar, Bring food into inner room, that I may eat from your hand. Tamar took cakes she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother in inner room.

familiar.text: And Amnon said unto Tamar, Bring the meat into the chamber, that I may eat of thine hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.

modern.text: Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat it from your hand.” Tamar took the cakes she had made and went to her brother Amnon’s bedroom.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַמְנ֜וֹן אֶל תָּמָ֗ר הָבִ֤יאִי הַבִּרְיָה֙ הַחֶ֔דֶר וְאֶבְרֶ֖ה מִיָּדֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֣ח תָּמָ֗ר אֶת הַלְּבִבוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔תָה וַתָּבֵ֛א לְאַמְנ֥וֹן אָחִ֖יהָ הֶחָֽדְרָה

verses.restored: She brought them near to him to eat. He seized her and said to her, Come, lie with me, my sister.

familiar.text: And when she had brought them unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said unto her, Come lie with me, my sister.

modern.text: And when she had brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her and said, “Come lie with me, my sister!”

original.text: וַתַּגֵּ֥שׁ אֵלָ֖יו לֶֽאֱכֹ֑ל וַיַּֽחֲזֶק בָּהּ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֔הּ בּ֛וֹאִי שִׁכְבִ֥י עִמִּ֖י אֲחוֹתִֽי

verses.restored: She said to him, No, my brother. Do not violate me, because such thing is not done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful folly.

familiar.text: And she answered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.

modern.text: “No, my brother!” she cried. “Do not humiliate me, for such a thing should never be done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אַל אָחִי֙ אַל תְּעַנֵּ֔נִי כִּ֛י לֹא יֵֽעָשֶׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַֽל תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה אֶת הַנְּבָלָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת

verses.restored: Where could I carry my shame? You would be like one of fools in Israel. Now please speak to king, because he will not withhold me from you.

familiar.text: And I, whither shall I cause my shame to go? and as for thee, thou shalt be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray thee, speak unto the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.

modern.text: Where could I ever take my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel! Please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”

original.text: וַאֲנִ֗י אָ֤נָה אוֹלִיךְ֙ אֶת חֶרְפָּתִ֔י וְאַתָּ֗ה תִּהְיֶ֛ה כְּאַחַ֥ד הַנְּבָלִ֖ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּה֙ דַּבֶּר נָ֣א אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִמְנָעֵ֖נִי מִמֶּֽךָּ

verses.restored: He was not willing to listen to her voice. He was stronger than she, violated her, and lay with her.

familiar.text: Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice: but, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.

modern.text: But Amnon refused to listen to her, and being stronger, he violated her and lay with her.

original.text: וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ בְּקוֹלָ֑הּ וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק מִמֶּ֨נָּה֙ וַיְעַנֶּ֔הָ וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב אֹתָֽהּ

verses.restored: Then Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, for hatred with which he hated her was greater than love with which he had claimed to love her. Amnon said to her, Rise, go.

familiar.text: Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so that the hatred wherewith he hated her was greater than the love wherewith he had loved her. And Amnon said unto her, Arise, be gone.

modern.text: Then Amnon hated Tamar with such intensity that his hatred was greater than the love he previously had. “Get up!” he said to her. “Be gone!”

original.text: וַיִּשְׂנָאֶ֣הָ אַמְנ֗וֹן שִׂנְאָה֙ גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י גְדוֹלָ֗ה הַשִּׂנְאָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׂנֵאָ֔הּ מֵאַהֲבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲהֵבָ֑הּ וַֽיֹּאמֶר לָ֥הּ אַמְנ֖וֹן ק֥וּמִי לֵֽכִי

verses.restored: She said to him, No—sending me away is a greater evil than the other you did to me. But he was not willing to listen to her.

familiar.text: And she said unto him, There is no cause: this evil in sending me away is greater than the other that thou didst unto me. But he would not hearken unto her.

modern.text: “No,” she replied, “sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!” But he refused to listen to her.

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אַל אוֹדֹ֞ת הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את מֵאַחֶ֛רֶת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֥יתָ עִמִּ֖י לְשַׁלְּחֵ֑נִי וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֥עַֽ לָֽהּ

verses.restored: He called his young servant who attended him and said, Please send this one out from me, outside, and bolt door after her.

familiar.text: Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put now this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.

modern.text: Instead, he called to his attendant and said, “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her!”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶֽת נַעֲרוֹ֙ מְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁלְחוּ נָ֥א אֶת זֹ֛את מֵעָלַ֖י הַח֑וּצָה וּנְעֹ֥ל הַדֶּ֖לֶת אַחֲרֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: She wore a long ornamented robe, for thus daughters of king who were virgins dressed. His servant brought her outside and bolted door after her.

familiar.text: And she had a garment of divers colours upon her: for with such robes were the king’s daughters that were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.

modern.text: So Amnon’s attendant threw her out and bolted the door behind her. Now Tamar was wearing a robe of many colors, because this is what the king’s virgin daughters wore.

original.text: וְעָלֶ֨יהָ֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת פַּסִּ֔ים כִּי֩ כֵ֨ן תִּלְבַּ֧שְׁןָ בְנוֹת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ הַבְּתוּלֹ֖ת מְעִילִ֑ים וַיֹּצֵ֨א אוֹתָ֤הּ מְשָֽׁרְתוֹ֙ הַח֔וּץ וְנָעַ֥ל הַדֶּ֖לֶת אַחֲרֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: Tamar placed ashes upon her head, tore long ornamented robe that was upon her, placed her hand upon her head, and walked, crying aloud as she went.

familiar.text: And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colours that was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on crying.

modern.text: And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her robe. And putting her hand on her head, she went away crying bitterly.

original.text: וַתִּקַּ֨ח תָּמָ֥ר אֵ֨פֶר֙ עַל רֹאשָׁ֔הּ וּכְתֹ֧נֶת הַפַּסִּ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלֶ֖יהָ קָרָ֑עָה וַתָּ֤שֶׂם יָדָהּ֙ עַל רֹאשָׁ֔הּ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ הָל֖וֹךְ וְזָעָֽקָה

verses.restored: Absalom her brother said to her, Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now, my sister, be silent; he is your brother. Do not set your heart on this thing. Tamar remained devastated/desolate in house of Absalom her brother.

familiar.text: And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? but hold now thy peace, my sister: he is thy brother; regard not this thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.

modern.text: Her brother Absalom said to her, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister. He is your brother. Do not take this thing to heart.” So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֜יהָ אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם אָחִ֗יהָ הַאֲמִינ֣וֹן אָחִיךְ֮ הָיָ֣ה עִמָּךְ֒ וְעַתָּ֞ה אֲחוֹתִ֤י הַחֲרִ֨ישִׁי֙ אָחִ֣יךְ ה֔וּא אַל תָּשִׁ֥יתִי אֶת לִבֵּ֖ךְ לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב תָּמָר֙ וְשֹׁ֣מֵמָ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם אָחִֽיהָ

verses.restored: King David heard all these things and became very angry.

familiar.text: But when king David heard of all these things, he was very wroth.

modern.text: When King David heard all this, he was furious.

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד שָׁמַ֕ע אֵ֥ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּ֥חַר ל֖וֹ מְאֹֽד

verses.restored: Absalom did not speak with Amnon either good or evil, because Absalom hated Amnon for violating Tamar his sister.

familiar.text: And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.

modern.text: And Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad, because he hated Amnon for disgracing his sister Tamar. Absalom’s Revenge on Amnon

original.text: וְלֹֽא דִבֶּ֧ר אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם עִם אַמְנ֖וֹן לְמֵרָ֣ע וְעַד ט֑וֹב כִּֽי שָׂנֵ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶת אַמְנ֔וֹן עַל דְּבַר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִנָּ֔ה אֵ֖ת תָּמָ֥ר אֲחֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: After two full years, Absalom had sheep-shearers at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all sons of king.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baalhazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.

modern.text: Two years later, when Absalom’s sheepshearers were at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, he invited all the sons of the king.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ לִשְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֔ים וַיִּהְי֤וּ גֹֽזְזִים֙ לְאַבְשָׁל֔וֹם בְּבַ֥עַל חָצ֖וֹר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִם אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיִּקְרָ֥א אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם לְכָל בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Absalom came to king and said, Look, your servant has sheep-shearers. Please let king and his servants go with your servant.

familiar.text: And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold now, thy servant hath sheepshearers; let the king, I beseech thee, and his servants go with thy servant.

modern.text: And he went to the king and said, “Your servant has just hired shearers. Will the king and his servants please come with me?”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה נָ֥א גֹזְזִ֖ים לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ יֵֽלֶךְ נָ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וַעֲבָדָ֖יו עִם עַבְדֶּֽךָ

familiar.text: And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him.

modern.text: “No, my son,” the king replied, “we should not all go, or we would be a burden to you.” Although Absalom urged him, he was not willing to go, but gave him his blessing.

familiar.text: Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go with thee?

modern.text: “If not,” said Absalom, “please let my brother Amnon go with us.” “Why should he go with you?” the king asked.

familiar.text: Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine, and when I say unto you, Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not: have not I commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant.

modern.text: Now Absalom had ordered his young men, “Watch Amnon until his heart is merry with wine, and when I order you to strike Amnon down, you are to kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!”

modern.text: Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

translation_notes: Amnon's fixation is not love. Desire that plots isolation, ignores refusal, uses force, and turns to hatred is entitlement and sexual violence.
Jonadab identifies a vulnerable access route and designs grooming through illness, family trust, caregiving labor, and royal command.
David orders Tamar into Amnon's house. The chapter gives no indication that he evaluates her safety or later provides justice.
Tamar says no repeatedly, names the act as violation and folly, reasons with Amnon, and proposes alternatives. Nothing she says or does constitutes consent.
Verse 14 must be translated plainly as rape/violation. Strength difference and refusal are explicit.
Amnon's hatred and expulsion are perpetrator behavior, not evidence that Tamar lost value or became shameful.
The servant who removes and locks out Tamar participates in institutional abandonment after violence.
Tamar's ashes, torn robe, hand on head, and public crying are survivor testimony. She is not responsible for family reputation.
Absalom gives her housing but also tells her to be silent and minimizes the matter. Shelter does not make silencing acceptable.
David becomes angry but takes no recorded protective or judicial action. Parental anger without accountability leaves the survivor unprotected.
Absalom's killing of Amnon is retaliatory execution after institutional failure, not survivor justice and not Tamar's responsibility.
The narrative follows male grief and political exile after verse 20; readers must resist allowing Tamar to disappear.
safety_note: Maximum anti-rape safeguards: Believe Tamar's explicit refusal. Do not call Amnon lovesick, blame Tamar's beauty, treat incest as the main harm rather than rape, demand survivor silence, praise revenge killing, or excuse David's inaction. Center survivor autonomy, trauma-informed care, public accountability, and protection from the perpetrator.
